## District travel guides in English

### Dhaka

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/dhaka
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Dhaka
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: The capital itself; easy to reach by bus, train and air from every part of the country
- Where to stay: Tk 3,000-10,000 (approx.) in Gulshan-Banani, mid-range hotels in Motijheel-Paltan Tk 1,500-3,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Kachchi biryani (layered mutton rice), bakarkhani (flaky flatbread), bakharkhani, morog polao (chicken pilaf) and Haji biryani
- Tips: Take a rickshaw to explore Old Dhaka, and on Fridays and holidays set out in the morning to avoid traffic jams

What to see:

1. Lalbagh Fort: An unfinished 17th-century Mughal fort; the tomb of Pari Bibi, a mosque and a museum
2. Ahsan Manzil: The pink palace of the Nawabs of Dhaka on the bank of the Buriganga, now a museum
3. National Parliament House: World-famous architecture designed by Louis Kahn; spend an afternoon by Crescent Lake
4. National Museum: The country's largest museum, in Shahbag; galleries from archaeology to the Liberation War, all under one roof
5. Sadarghat & Old Dhaka: The bustle of the launch terminal, the Star Mosque, Shankhari Bazar and Old Dhaka's kachchi and bakarkhani
6. Ramna Park: The city's green lungs; the Pohela Boishakh Batamul (banyan tree) and the Swadhinata Stambha (Independence Monument)

### Faridpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/faridpur
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Faridpur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 3-4 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Fulbaria), quick to reach via the Padma Bridge
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Madhumati Express, Sundarban Express, Benapole Express, Jahanabad Express and Ruposhi Bangla Express
- Dhaka to Faridpur train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-faridpur
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Faridpur's date palm juice, chomchom (milk sweet) and other sweets
- Tips: Go in winter, the date palm juice season, for a taste of the countryside

What to see:

1. Baishrashi Zamindar Bari: An old zamindar house in Baishrashi village, Sadarpur; locally also known as Rajendra Babu's house
2. Padma River Ghat: Wide chars (sandbanks) along the Padma, boat trips and a place to watch the sunset
3. Jasimuddin's Home: Gobindapur, birthplace of Palli Kabi (the rural poet) Jasimuddin, and places linked to his memory
4. Mathurapur Deul: An ancient temple and structure built of old bricks; a historic monument
5. Pathrail Mosque: A multi-domed Sultanate-era mosque at Pathrail in Bhanga, also known as the Majlish Aulia Mosque; a huge pond beside it
6. Satoir Mosque: A 16th-century nine-domed mosque in Satoir village, Boalmari, believed to date from the reign of Sultan Husain Shah

### Gazipur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/gazipur
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Gazipur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 1-2 hours by bus (from Mohakhali/Gabtoli), about an hour by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Tista Express, Bhrammaputra Express, Jamuna Express, Jamalpur Express, Hawr Express, Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Nilsagar Express, Chilahati Express, Lalmoni Express, Silkcity Express, Padma Express, Dhumketu Express and Chitra Express
- Dhaka to Gazipur train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-gazipur
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Joydebpur and Tongi Tk 1,000-2,500 (approx.), resorts Tk 3,000-8,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Jackfruit, Joydebpur's sweets and Bhawal's pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: For a day trip, set off early; the Safari Park gets very crowded on holidays

What to see:

1. Bhawal National Park: A national park ringed by sal forest; the best place near Dhaka for picnics and walks
2. Bangabandhu Safari Park: A safari to see lions, tigers and deer up close, with a huge open area
3. Rajendrapur National Park: Sal forest like Madhupur's, natural surroundings and picnic spots
4. Nuhash Polli: The garden house tied to the memory of Humayun Ahmed, at Pirujali in Gazipur
5. Bhawal Rajbari: The huge palace of the Bhawal zamindars in Gazipur town; linked to the famous Bhawal Sannyasi case
6. Nagori Church: A church built by the Portuguese in 1664 at Nagori, Kaliganj; the first grammar and dictionary of the Bangla language were written here

### Gopalganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/gopalganj
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Gopalganj
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), or 3 hours via the Padma Bridge
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Jahanabad Express and Ruposhi Bangla Express
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Gopalganj's rasmalai (cheese balls in cream), chomchom (milk sweet) and other sweets
- Tips: It gets crowded in March and at the time of the Orakandi festival, so arrange your stay in advance

What to see:

1. Bangabandhu Mausoleum: The tomb complex of the Father of the Nation, with a museum and library; beside the Baigar River
2. Orakandi Thakurbari: The holy seat of the Matua community; hundreds of thousands come to the Baruni bathing fair in Chaitra (March-April)
3. Ujani Zamindar Bari: Ruins of an old zamindar house and a temple in Muksudpur
4. Madhumati River: The river flowing past the town and a British-era canal; afternoons on a boat
5. Sukanta Bhattacharya's Ancestral Home: The ancestral home of Sukanta Bhattacharya, poet of 'Chharpatra', in Unshia village, Kotalipara

### Kishoreganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/kishoreganj
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Kishoreganj
- Best time: June to October (for the haor in the monsoon), November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 3-4 hours by bus (from Mohakhali), 4 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Egarosindhur Provati, Egarosindhur Godhuli, Kishorganj Express, Mahanagar Provati/Godhuli, Mohanagar Express, Turna, Chattala Express, Parabat Express and Upaban Express
- Dhaka to Kishoreganj train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-kishoreganj
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Kishoreganj's pabda fish, yoghurt and fresh fish from the haor
- Tips: In the monsoon, bargain over the boat fare at Nikli before you set off, and keep a life jacket with you

What to see:

1. Egarosindur: A historic port on the bank of the Brahmaputra, linked to the memory of Isa Khan
2. Nikli Haor: A green haor (wetland) awash with water in the monsoon, famous for boat trips and migratory birds
3. Itna and Astagram Haor: A vast haor area: sea-like expanses of water in the monsoon, and the life of fishers
4. Sholakia Eidgah: One of the largest Eid prayer grounds in the subcontinent, where hundreds of thousands of people pray
5. Jangalbari Fort: Ruins of a fort from Isa Khan's rule, a relic of the history of the Baro Bhuiyan (twelve chieftains)

### Madaripur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/madaripur
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Madaripur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 2-3 hours by bus (from Sayedabad/Gabtoli), quick via the Padma Bridge
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Madhumati Express
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Madaripur's hilsa, cow's milk sweets and yoghurt
- Tips: You can see it in a day; best in the hilsa season (September-October)

What to see:

1. Shakuni Lake: A huge lake in the middle of town, with walking paths and afternoon hangouts
2. Auliapur Neelkuthi: The house of British indigo planters, with memories of the Great Bengal Famine of 1770 and the peasant revolt
3. Shah Madar Dargah: The shrine of the saint Madaripur is named after, in the town centre
4. Padma Bridge Shibchar: The vastness of the Padma from the Jajira-Shibchar end of the bridge
5. Rajaram Temple, Khalia: A two-storey temple built by zamindar Rajaram Roy Chowdhury at Khalia, Rajoir; designs from the Ramayana and Mahabharata cover its walls; a protected antiquity

### Manikganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/manikganj
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Manikganj
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 2-3 hours by bus (from Gabtoli)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Manikganj's ghol (buttermilk) and milk sweets
- Tips: You can go from Dhaka and come back in a day; set out early

What to see:

1. Baliati Zamindar Bari: Baliati Palace in Saturia, now a museum and a popular film shooting location
2. Teota Zamindar Bari: The zamindars' huge old palace at Teota, Shibalaya
3. Dhankora Zamindar Bari: An old zamindar house in Dhankora village, Saturia; lion sculptures at the entrance and a huge mansion
4. Aricha Ghat: The vast river at Aricha Ghat and the experience of watching the ferries
5. Matta Math: A tall math (tower temple), about 250 years old, beside a pond in Manikganj Sadar

### Munshiganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/munshiganj
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Munshiganj
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 1-2 hours by bus (from Gulistan/Sayedabad), on the Padma Bridge route
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Madhumati Express
- Where to stay: Basic hotels around Mawa, Tk 1,000-2,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Mawa's fried hilsa, Munshiganj's bananas and potatoes
- Tips: On the Padma Bridge route, stop for hilsa at Mawa Ghat; it gets very crowded on holidays

What to see:

1. Idrakpur Fort: A small Mughal fort built by Mir Jumla, right in the middle of town
2. Mawa Ghat: The Dhaka end of the Padma Bridge; fresh fried hilsa at the ghat and sunsets over the river
3. Bikrampur Museum: A thousand years of Bikrampur's history and the memory of Atish Dipankar
4. Sonarang Twin Temples: Two tall 18th-century brick temples side by side in Tongibari
5. Bajrajogini: The village of the Buddhist scholar Atish; an ancient monastery (vihara) found in excavations

### Narayanganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/narayanganj
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Narayanganj
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 1-2 hours by bus or CNG auto-rickshaw (from Gulistan/Jatrabari)
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Sonargaon and in town, Tk 1,200-3,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Narayanganj's hilsa, bhorta (mashed relishes) and Sonargaon's sweets
- Tips: You can see Panam Nagar and the museum in a day; it is best to go in the morning

What to see:

1. Panam Nagar, Sonargaon: An abandoned medieval trading town; a famous street lined with two rows of old buildings
2. Folk Art Museum, Sonargaon: A museum of folk art and crafts founded by Zainul Abedin
3. Mazar of Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah: A historic Sultanate-era tomb in Sonargaon
4. Banglar Taj Mahal: A building modelled on the Taj Mahal, near Sonargaon
5. Shitalakshya River: Boat trips along the river and the town's traditional ghats

### Narsingdi

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/narsingdi
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Narsingdi
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 1 hour 30 minutes by train (from Kamalapur), 2 hours by bus
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Mahanagar Provati/Godhuli, Mohanagar Express, Chattala Express, Upakul Express, Egarosindhur Provati, Egarosindhur Godhuli and Kishorganj Express
- Dhaka to Narsingdi train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-narsingdi
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Local food near the Madhabdi cloth market, and Narsingdi's sweets
- Tips: Take a local guide at Wari-Bateshwar to understand the history better

What to see:

1. Wari-Bateshwar: An archaeological site about 2,000 years old, evidence of an ancient city in Bangladesh
2. Belabo Countryside: The rural natural beauty of the Brahmaputra and its riverbanks
3. Madhabdi Textile Area: The area around Madhabdi and Palash, famous for textiles and handloom weaving
4. Panchdona Riverside: Village life on the banks of the Meghna and the Shitalakshya
5. Bir Sreshtho Matiur Rahman Museum: A museum and library opened in 2008 at Ramnagar, Raipura, in memory of Bir Sreshtho Flight Lieutenant Matiur Rahman
6. Dream Holiday Park: A big amusement park in Sadar upazila; a place to spend the whole day with family and go on rides

### Rajbari

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/rajbari
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Rajbari
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 3-4 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), about 2.5 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Madhumati Express, Sundarban Express and Benapole Express
- Dhaka to Rajbari train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-rajbari
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Rajbari's hilsa, yoghurt and sweets
- Tips: Go to Goalanda Ghat in the afternoon to see the Padma and the Jamuna meet from a boat

What to see:

1. Goalanda Ghat: Where the Padma and the Jamuna meet; the ghat's traditional Goalanda chicken curry
2. Daulatdia Ghat: A huge ferry ghat on the Padma; fresh river hilsa and ferry crossings
3. Nalia Twin Temples: Two old temples side by side in Baliakandi, with terracotta work
4. Padamdi: The grave and memorial centre of Mir Mosharraf Hossain, author of 'Bishad Sindhu', at Padamdi
5. Samadhinagar Math: Samadhinagar Math in Jangal union, Baliakandi upazila, also known as Anadi Ashram

### Shariatpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/shariatpur
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Shariatpur
- Best time: September to November (hilsa season), October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 2-3 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), via the Padma Bridge
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town and in Jajira, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Padma hilsa, bhapa ilish (steamed hilsa) and shorshe ilish (hilsa in mustard)
- Tips: There are traffic jams around the Padma Bridge on holidays, so set off in the morning

What to see:

1. Padma Bridge Jajira: The southern end of the bridge; riverside restaurants and afternoons at Naodoba
2. Mahisar Dighi: A huge ancient pond and a temple in Bhedarganj
3. Rudrakar Math: A 19th-century zamindar house in Sadar, with a beautiful terracotta math (tower temple)
4. Sureshwar Darbar: A famous darbar (Sufi shrine) on the bank of the Padma in Naria; huge crowds at the urs (annual festival)
5. Dhanuka Manasa Bari: The ancient Manasa temple of Mayur Bhatta's house in Dhanuka village, Sadar, and several more temples; a protected antiquity

### Tangail

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/tangail
- Division: Dhaka Division
- District town: Tangail
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 2-3 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Mohakhali)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Lalmoni Express, Silkcity Express, Padma Express, Chitra Express, Jamalpur Express, Nilsagar Express, Rangpur Express and Dhumketu Express
- Dhaka to Tangail train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-tangail
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Tangail's chomchom (milk sweet), Porabari's sweets and saris
- Tips: When buying Tangail saris, compare prices at the market

What to see:

1. Atia Mosque: A beautiful Mughal-era mosque decorated with terracotta, built in 1609
2. Madhupur National Park: Vast sal forest, areas of the Indigenous Garo people, and hill trails
3. Dhanbari Nawab Bari: An old palace from the time of Nawab Ali Chowdhury
4. Karatia Zamindar Bari: The palace of the famous Panni zamindar family, and Saadat College
5. Bangabandhu Bridge Area: See the country's great bridge and the ghats of the Jamuna River

### Bandarban

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/bandarban
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Bandarban
- Best time: October to March, July to September to see the waterfalls in the monsoon
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 9-10 hours by bus (from Kalabagan/Sayedabad), the night bus is convenient
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town Tk 1,200-3,500 (approx.), resorts Tk 3,000-8,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Bamboo biryani (cooked in bamboo tubes), hill-style bhorta (mashed relishes) and Indigenous food
- Tips: Trekking in Bandarban needs permission from the administration and a local guide; book your chander gari (open-top jeep) in advance

What to see:

1. Nilgiri: A hill about 2,200 feet above sea level, a popular place to watch the clouds and the sunset
2. Nafakhum Waterfall: A waterfall on the Nafa river near Thanchi, reached by trekking
3. Boga Lake: A natural lake on a hilltop in Ruma upazila, and a Tripura village (para)
4. Keokradong: One of the highest hills in Bangladesh, reached by trekking from Ruma
5. Golden Temple (Buddha Dhatu Jadi): A large Buddhist temple in Bandarban Sadar, with a golden Buddha statue
6. Chimbuk Hill: A hill on the Bandarban-Cox's Bazar road, a popular spot for views of clouds and valleys

### Brahmanbaria

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/brahmanbaria
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Brahmanbaria
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 2-3 hours by train (from Kamalapur), 3-4 hours by bus
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Mahanagar Provati/Godhuli, Mohanagar Express, Turna, Chattala Express, Upakul Express, Parabat Express, Jayentika Express and Kalni Express
- Dhaka to Brahmanbaria train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-brahmanbaria
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 800-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Brahmanbaria's chhana (cottage cheese) sweets, jhal morog (spicy chicken) and pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: A day trip by train is easy; agree the boat fare on the Titas in advance

What to see:

1. Titas River: A river famous for the life of the Malo community and for boat trips
2. Akhaura Land Port: A busy land port on the Indian border, and a historic railway station
3. Akhaura Liberation War Site: Memories of the Akhaura battlefront of the Liberation War
4. Kasba Historic Mosque: An old mosque and historic architecture
5. Kal Bhairab Temple: A temple in the district town, famous for its Kal Bhairab idol, about 28 feet tall
6. Arifail Mosque: A three-domed mosque from 1662 in Arifail village, Sarail; listed by the Department of Archaeology

### Chandpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/chandpur
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Chandpur
- Best time: September to November (hilsa), October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by launch (from Sadarghat), 2-3 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), 2 hours 30 minutes by train
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Chandpur's fried hilsa, bhapa ilish (steamed hilsa) and shorshe ilish (hilsa in mustard)
- Tips: In the hilsa season, book your hotel in advance and enjoy the trip by launch

What to see:

1. Meghna-Padma Confluence: Where two rivers meet, famous for afternoon boat rides and hilsa
2. Chandpur Hilsa Market: The country's top hilsa market; a chance to buy fresh hilsa in season
3. Chandpur Riverside: Afternoon hangouts and food on the town's riverbank
4. Hajiganj Mosque: An old, traditional mosque and its architecture
5. Lohagarh Math: Two huge maths (tower temples) built by the Lohagarh zamindars beside the Dakatia River in Faridganj
6. Rupsha Zamindar Bari: A zamindar house built about 250 years ago at Rupsha, Faridganj

### Chattogram

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/chattogram
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Chattogram
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by train (from Kamalapur), 6-7 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), 50 minutes by air
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Suborno Express, Sonar Bangla Express, Mahanagar Provati/Godhuli, Mohanagar Express, Turna, Chattala Express, Cox's Bazar Express and Parjotak Express
- Dhaka to Chattogram train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-chattogram
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in GEC/Agrabad, Tk 1,500-4,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Mezbani beef (feast-style beef curry), Chattogram's bhuna khichuri (spiced rice and lentils) and shutki (dried fish)
- Tips: For mezbani food, look for a local restaurant; the beach is best in the afternoon

What to see:

1. Patenga Beach: The city's most popular beach, near the mouth of the Karnaphuli
2. Foy's Lake: A lake ringed by hills and an amusement park in Khulshi, good for a family outing
3. Batali Hill and War Cemetery: The graves of Second World War soldiers, and a high point of the city
4. Ethnological Museum: A collection on the cultures of the Indigenous hill peoples
5. Sitakunda Ecopark and Chandranath Dham: Waterfalls in the hills, an eco park and the Hindu pilgrimage site of Chandranath Temple
6. Karnaphuli River: Sampan boat rides on the Karnaphuli, and a look at the port city's ship docks

### Cox's Bazar

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/coxs-bazar
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Cox's Bazar
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 9-10 hours by bus (from Sayedabad/Kalabagan), 1 hour 10 minutes by air, 8 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Cox's Bazar Express and Parjotak Express
- Dhaka to Cox's Bazar train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-coxsbazar
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in the beach area Tk 2,000-6,000 (approx.), luxury Tk 10,000+ (approx.)
- What to eat: Shutki (dried fish), fried loitta and churi fish (Bombay duck and ribbonfish) and Cox's Bazar seafood
- Tips: For Saint Martin's, arrange the ship and permit in advance; when swimming at the beach, follow the lifeguards and flags

What to see:

1. Cox's Bazar Sea Beach: The world's longest natural sandy sea beach, about 120 kilometres long
2. Inani Beach: A beautiful, quiet beach of rocky coral and blue water, 32 km from Cox's Bazar town
3. Himchari: A beach framed by hills and waterfalls, about 12 km from Cox's Bazar
4. Saint Martin's Island: Bangladesh's only coral island, reached by ship from Teknaf
5. Maheshkhali: An island famous for the Adinath Temple and betel leaf farming, reached by ferry
6. Ramu Buddhist Temple: An old 17th-century Buddhist monastery (vihara) and a huge Buddha statue

### Cumilla

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/cumilla
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Cumilla
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 2-3 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), 2-3 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Mahanagar Provati/Godhuli, Mohanagar Express, Turna, Chattala Express and Upakul Express
- Dhaka to Cumilla train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-cumilla
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Cumilla's rasmalai (cheese balls in cream), Matribhandar's sweets and khadi cloth
- Tips: Go to Matribhandar to buy rasmalai; you can see it all, Mainamati included, in a single day

What to see:

1. Shalban Vihara, Mainamati: The vast ruins of an ancient Buddhist monastery (vihara) from the 7th-8th centuries
2. Mainamati Museum: A collection of ancient terracotta and metal objects found in excavations
3. Kotila Mura: Three mounds of ancient Buddhist stupas near Mainamati
4. Dharmasagar Dighi: A big historic pond in the middle of town, a popular place for an afternoon stroll
5. Comilla War Cemetery: A well-kept cemetery of Second World War soldiers

### Feni

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/feni
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Feni
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), 4 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Mahanagar Provati/Godhuli, Mohanagar Express, Turna and Chattala Express
- Dhaka to Feni train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-feni
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Feni's khaja (flaky sweet), pitha (rice cakes) and local bhorta (mashed relishes)
- Tips: On the way to Chattogram, you can stop for a day and see Feni

What to see:

1. Muhuri Project: A huge reservoir and sluice gates, a popular afternoon picnic spot
2. Feni River: A river running along the Indian border, and village scenes on its banks
3. Liberation War Memorial: A place that keeps alive the memory of the war of 1971
4. Sonagazi Coast: A rural coast on the Bay of Bengal, and fishing villages
5. Bijoy Singh Dighi: A huge 37.5-acre pond in front of the Circuit House, about 2 km west of town; rows of trees line its high banks
6. Shamsher Gazi's Dighi & Tunnel: Memories of the 18th-century hero Shamsher Gazi at Jagannath Sonapur and Champaknagar in Chhagalnaiya: a pond and a secret tunnel
7. Pratappur Zamindar Bari: A zamindar house built around 1760 in Daganbhuiyan; 10 buildings and 13 ponds spread over 13 acres
8. Sharshadi Shahi Mosque: An old royal (shahi) mosque in Sharshadi village, Sadar upazila; known locally as the Takiyah Mosque
9. Parshuram Rubber Garden: A rubber plantation in Parshuram upazila, on the Indian border; shady paths between rows of rubber trees

### Khagrachhari

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/khagrachhari
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Khagrachhari
- Best time: October to March, July to September to see the waterfalls in the monsoon
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 7-8 hours by bus (from Kalabagan/Sayedabad)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town Tk 800-2,000 (approx.), resorts in Sajek Tk 1,500-4,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Hill food cooked in bamboo tubes, Indigenous bhorta (mashed relishes) and jackfruit
- Tips: To go to Sajek, travel with the security forces' morning convoy and carry your ID card

What to see:

1. Alutila Cave: A mysterious tunnel inside the hill; you need a torch to go in
2. Richhang Waterfall: A beautiful waterfall in the hills of Mahalchhari, at its best in the monsoon
3. Sajek Valley: Sajek, known as the kingdom of clouds; it is in Rangamati district, but you get there through Khagrachhari
4. Toini Waterfall: Natural scenery of Indigenous villages and hill streams in Khagrachhari
5. Khagrachhari Town: The heritage of a hill town, Indigenous markets and culture

### Lakshmipur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/lakshmipur
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Lakshmipur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), 5 hours by launch and bus combined
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Lakshmipur's hilsa, fish from the Meghna and village pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: Before going out to the chars, check the boat times and the tides

What to see:

1. Meghna Riverbank: The wide banks of the Meghna; afternoon boat trips and the river breeze
2. Raipur Market: The area's traditional trading centre and local market
3. Char Alexander: Chars (river islands) at the mouth of the Meghna, and a quiet coast on the Bay of Bengal
4. Dalal Bazar Zamindar Bari: Heritage buildings from the old zamindari era
5. Khoasagar Dighi: A huge ancient pond near the Dalal Bazar zamindar house
6. Jiner Mosque, Raipur: A mosque built in 1888 in Raipur, also known as Masjid-e-Jame Abdullah; many visit to see its unique architecture

### Noakhali

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/noakhali
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Noakhali
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), and for Nijhum Dwip, Sonapur/Hatiya trawlers and speedboats
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Upakul Express
- Dhaka to Noakhali train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-noakhali
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town Tk 700-2,000 (approx.), resorts on Nijhum Dwip Tk 2,000-5,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Noakhali's sea fish, prawns and shutki bhorta (mashed dried fish)
- Tips: For Nijhum Dwip, check the tide times before you hire a trawler, and book your resort in advance

What to see:

1. Nijhum Dwip: An island at the mouth of the Meghna, famous for its keora (mangrove) forest and deer
2. Hatiya Island: A large island upazila at the mouth of the Meghna; the life of fishers and river views
3. Subarnachar: Newly risen char land; farming and the variety of village life
4. Basurhat Bazar: The town's traditional market and local culture
5. Gandhi Ashram, Joyag: An ashram linked to the memory of Mahatma Gandhi's peace mission of 1946

### Rangamati

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/rangamati
- Division: Chattogram Division
- District town: Rangamati
- Best time: October to March, the lake is green in the monsoon
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Kalabagan/Sayedabad)
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town Tk 1,000-3,000 (approx.), resorts in Sajek Tk 1,500-4,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Hill food cooked in bamboo tubes, fish from Kaptai and Indigenous bhorta (mashed relishes)
- Tips: Bargain over speedboat or boat hire on the lake beforehand; travel to Sajek with the security convoy

What to see:

1. Kaptai Lake: A huge man-made lake on the Karnaphuli River, the best place for boat trips
2. Hanging Bridge: The hanging bridge over Kaptai Lake, a symbol of Rangamati
3. Shuvolong Waterfall: A waterfall that is especially beautiful in the monsoon, reached by boat
4. Rajbana Vihara: Rangamati's main Buddhist monastery (vihara), and the heritage of the Chakma king
5. Sajek Valley: A cloud-wrapped hill tourism area at the Ruilui and Konglak villages (paras)
6. Tribal Museum: A collection on the life and culture of the hill peoples, including the Chakma and Marma

### Bogura

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/bogura
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Bogura
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), 6-7 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Lalmoni Express, Rangpur Express, Burimari Express, Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Panchagarh Express, Nilsagar Express, Chilahati Express and Kurigram Express
- Dhaka to Bogura train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-bogura
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Bogura town, Tk 1,200-3,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Bogura's doi (yoghurt), kotkoti (crunchy sweet) and jhal pitha (spicy rice cakes)
- Tips: You can see Mahasthangarh and Gokul Medh in one day; set off early

What to see:

1. Mahasthangarh: The ruins of Bangladesh's oldest fortified city, Pundranagar, on the bank of the Karatoya River
2. Gokul Medh: The mound of an ancient Buddhist stupa near Mahasthangarh, popularly known as Behula's Bashor Ghar (bridal chamber)
3. Vasu Bihar: Ruins of an ancient Buddhist monastery (vihara) in Shibganj, in peaceful surroundings
4. Kherua Mosque: A beautiful Mughal-era mosque decorated with terracotta, in Sherpur
5. Bogura Nawab Bari: The historic palace of the Nawab family in Bogura town, now a protected building
6. Mahasthan Museum: A collection of ancient coins, terracotta plaques and artefacts found at Mahasthangarh

### Chapainawabganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/chapainawabganj
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Chapainawabganj
- Best time: May to July (mango season), November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), about 6 hours by train (Banalata Express)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Banalata Express
- Dhaka to Chapainawabganj train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-chapainawabganj
- Where to stay: Basic to mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Mangoes, amsotto (dried mango sheets) and Chapai's sweets
- Tips: In the mango season, book your hotel in advance; carry your ID card in the border area

What to see:

1. Chhota Sona Mosque: A historic Sultanate-era mosque with 11 domes, in the Gaur area of Shibganj
2. Kotwali Darwaza: The huge brick gateway of the ancient fort of Gaur
3. Mango Orchards of Shibganj: Orchards of thousands of mango trees in season, famous for Chapai's Fazli and Langra mangoes
4. Mahananda River: The river that flows right past the town; enjoy an afternoon boat ride and the atmosphere of the ghats
5. Sonamasjid Land Port: A land port on the Indian border, right next to the archaeological sites of Gaur

### Joypurhat

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/joypurhat
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Joypurhat
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 6-7 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Panchagarh Express, Nilsagar Express, Chilahati Express and Kurigram Express
- Dhaka to Joypurhat train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-joypurhat
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Joypurhat's yoghurt and pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: Keep the trip short; it is best planned together with Bogura or Naogaon

What to see:

1. Achranga Dighi: A huge ancient pond in Khetlal; migratory birds in winter
2. Nandail Dighi: A pond and ghat in Kalai, nearly a thousand years old
3. Hinda Kasba Mosque: An ornate 19th-century mosque in Khetlal
4. Patharghata: Ruins of an ancient city and temples in Panchbibi
5. Lakma Zamindar Bari: A zamindar house known as Chowdhury Bari in Koria village, Panchbibi; with the palace are an elephant stable, a horse stable and an estate office (kachari)
6. Gopinathpur Temple: A temple about 500 years old at Gopinathpur, Akkelpur; a fair is held at Dol Purnima (the spring full moon)

### Naogaon

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/naogaon
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Naogaon
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), 6-7 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Drutojan Express and Nilsagar Express
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Naogaon Sadar, Tk 1,000-2,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Naogaon's rice, pitha (rice cakes) and mangoes
- Tips: Paharpur and Altadighi can be seen in one day; hire a vehicle

What to see:

1. Paharpur Buddhist Vihara: A UNESCO World Heritage Site in Badalgachhi, one of the largest Buddhist monasteries (viharas) in the subcontinent
2. Kusumba Mosque: A 16th-century mosque built of black stone at Kusumba, Manda
3. Altadighi National Park: Sal forest around a huge pond in Dhamoirhat, and a picnic spot
4. Jagaddal Vihara: The archaeological site of an ancient Buddhist monastery (vihara) in Dhamoirhat
5. Sapahar Mango and Kul: Famous for the mango orchards and apple kul (jujube) of the Sapahar area

### Natore

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/natore
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Natore
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 5 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Panchagarh Express, Nilsagar Express, Chilahati Express, Lalmoni Express, Rangpur Express, Burimari Express, Kurigram Express, Silkcity Express, Padma Express and Dhumketu Express
- Dhaka to Natore train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-natore
- Where to stay: Basic to mid-range hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Kanchagolla (fresh cheese sweet) and Natore's yoghurt
- Tips: Check Uttara Ganabhaban's visiting hours and closing days before you go

What to see:

1. Uttara Ganabhaban: The Dighapatia Rajbari, now a government residence (Ganabhaban); a beautiful palace and gardens
2. Natore Rajbari: A historic palace linked to the memory of Rani Bhabani
3. Chalan Beel: A huge beel (wetland), popular for boat trips across its vast waters in the monsoon
4. Natore Kanchagolla: Natore's world-famous sweet; buy it straight from the shops in town
5. Halti Beel: A huge beel (wetland) in Naldanga; in the monsoon, water brims on both sides of the Patul-Khajura road and villages look like islands, and the crowds grow
6. Shahid Sagar: The memorial to the massacre of 5 May 1971 at North Bengal Sugar Mills, and the pond itself; a museum beside it

### Pabna

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/pabna
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Pabna
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 4-5 hours by train (via Ishwardi)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Drutojan Express, Chilahati Express, Silkcity Express, Padma Express, Dhumketu Express, Madhumati Express and Chitra Express
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town and in Ishwardi, Tk 1,000-2,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Pabna's yoghurt and ghee
- Tips: You need permission to go inside the Rooppur project; it is easier to see it from outside

What to see:

1. Hardinge Bridge: A century-old railway bridge over the Padma at Pakshi, with the road bridge beside it; stunning at sunset
2. Satsang Ashram: The birthplace and ashram of Sree Sree Thakur Anukulchandra
3. Jor Bangla Temple: An 18th-century terracotta temple in the town
4. Pakshi: The Pakshi railway colony and the chars of the Padma; the town of the Rooppur project
5. Chalan Beel: A beel (wetland) like a sea in the monsoon; sunsets from a boat

### Rajshahi

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/rajshahi
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Rajshahi
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), 5-6 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Silkcity Express, Padma Express, Dhumketu Express, Madhumati Express and Banalata Express
- Dhaka to Rajshahi train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-rajshahi
- Where to stay: Mid-range to good hotels in the city, Tk 1,500-5,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Rajshahi's mangoes, silk, sweets and Padma hilsa
- Tips: You can cover Puthia and Bagha in one day; hire a car from the city

What to see:

1. Puthia Temple Complex: The terracotta-decorated temple cluster of the Puthia palace, with the Govinda and Shiva temples
2. Varendra Research Museum: One of the country's oldest museums, with a collection of sculptures from the Pala and Sena periods
3. Padma Garden: A landscaped leisure park on the bank of the Padma, and a place for afternoon hangouts
4. Bagha Shahi Mosque: A 16th-century terracotta-decorated mosque in Bagha upazila, and the pond beside it
5. Shah Makhdum Dargah: A historic dargah (shrine) in Rajshahi city, close to the Padma
6. Rajshahi University Campus: A green, open campus where you can see migratory birds in winter

### Sirajganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/sirajganj
- Division: Rajshahi Division
- District town: Sirajganj
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 3-4 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 4-5 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Lalmoni Express, Silkcity Express, Padma Express, Dhumketu Express, Sirajganj Express and Chitra Express
- Dhaka to Sirajganj train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-sirajganj
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Sirajganj's yoghurt and fish from the Jamuna
- Tips: Shahzadpur is some way from the town; set off early and you can see it all in a day

What to see:

1. Rabindra Kachari Bari, Shahzadpur: The zamindari estate office (kachari bari) and museum linked to the memory of Rabindranath Tagore
2. Bangabandhu Jamuna Bridge: One of the country's longest bridges, over the Jamuna; great sunset views
3. Makhdum Shah Daula Dargah: A historic shrine and mosque in Shahzadpur
4. Chalan Beel: A vast beel (wetland) in the Tarash and Ullapara area; boat trips in the monsoon
5. Hard Point: Part of the town protection embankment on the Jamuna, beside the town; every afternoon crowds gather for the river breeze and the sunset
6. Hatikumrul Navaratna Temple: An ancient navaratna (nine-spired) temple at Hatikumrul, Ullapara; the largest of the navaratna temples found in the country

### Bagerhat

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/bagerhat
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Bagerhat
- Best time: November to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge); 45 minutes from Khulna
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town Tk 800-2,000 (approx.); a Parjatan (tourism) motel in Mongla
- What to eat: Chuijhal meat (cooked with a spicy vine), narkel naru (coconut sweet balls)
- Tips: Visit the Sixty Dome Mosque in the morning; in the afternoon you can see Mongla and go back to Khulna

What to see:

1. Sixty Dome Mosque: A UNESCO World Heritage Site; a huge 15th-century mosque with 77 domes, built by Khan Jahan Ali
2. Khan Jahan Ali Mazar: Freshwater crocodiles in the pond beside the shrine; crowds of visitors every day
3. Nine Dome Mosque: A small mosque with superb terracotta work, on the west bank of Thakur Dighi
4. Bagerhat Museum: Next to the Sixty Dome Mosque; finds from the excavated city of Khalifatabad, and its history
5. Mongla & Sundarbans: Karamjal and Harbaria by trawler from Mongla; a look at the country's second seaport
6. Kodla Math: A tall 17th-century brick math (tower temple) in Ayodhya village; terracotta designs

### Chuadanga

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/chuadanga
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Chuadanga
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge), by train to Chuadanga station
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Chitra Express, Sundarban Express and Benapole Express
- Dhaka to Chuadanga train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-chuadanga
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Chuadanga's date palm molasses (khejur gur), maize
- Tips: On the Kushtia-Meherpur route, you can take in Chuadanga in a day

What to see:

1. Darshana & Keru: A British-era sugar mill and the country's only distillery; the Indian border on the railway line
2. Gholdari Mosque: A Sultanate-era mosque from 1006 AH (Hijri) in Alamdanga
3. Mathabhanga River: A calm river beside the town; the sunset from the bridge in the late afternoon
4. Tiarbila Mosque: A small three-domed Mughal-era mosque, Alamdanga
5. Aat Kabar: The graves of eight freedom fighters martyred in 1971, at Natudah in Damurhuda; beside them, an open-air stage and a Liberation War museum
6. Karpasdanga Neelkuthi: A British-era indigo planters' house (neelkuthi) on the bank of the Bhairab River in Damurhuda; an old cemetery of English officials nearby

### Jashore

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/jashore
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Jashore
- Best time: December to February (flower season)
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge), by train on the Benapole Express, and there are flights too
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Chitra Express, Sundarban Express, Benapole Express, Ruposhi Bangla Express and Jahanabad Express
- Dhaka to Jashore train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-jashore
- Where to stay: Hotels in town, Tk 1,000-3,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Jashore's date palm molasses (khejur gur) and patali (date palm jaggery), Jamtala's sweets
- Tips: Go to Gadkhali at dawn; after 9 o'clock the flowers are cut and loaded onto trucks

What to see:

1. Sagardari: The birthplace of the poet Michael Madhusudan Dutt, with a museum, on the bank of the Kopotakkho River; the Madhu Mela fair in January
2. Gadkhali Flower Market: The country's flower capital; at dawn, fields full of roses, marigolds and gerberas, and the flower market
3. Benapole Land Port: The busiest land port on the Indian border; you can watch the border retreat ceremony
4. Chanchra Shiva Temple: The heritage of Bangladesh's first district; the 17th-century Chanchra temple
5. Bharat Bhayna: The mound of an ancient Buddhist stupa in Keshabpur; terracotta finds from the excavations

### Jhenaidah

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/jhenaidah
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Jhenaidah
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 3.5-4 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Chitra Express, Sundarban Express and Benapole Express
- Where to stay: Hotels in town, Tk 800-2,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Jhenaidah's date palm molasses (khejur gur), chhanar jilapi (cheese jalebi)
- Tips: You can see the Barobazar mosques in an afternoon by auto-rickshaw

What to see:

1. Naldanga Rajbari: Ruins of an old palace and temples in Kaliganj; now a resort and picnic spot
2. Miar Dalan: A 19th-century zamindar house on the bank of the Nabaganga River, close to town
3. Barobazar Mosques: Ruins of several Sultanate-era mosques at Barobazar
4. Johan Dream Valley: A theme park with rides, for a full day out with the family
5. Shailkupa Shahi Mosque: A 16th-century mosque and shrine on the bank of the Kumar River

### Khulna

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/khulna
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Khulna
- Best time: November to February (best for the Sundarbans)
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge, from Gabtoli/Sayedabad), by train on the Sundarban Express
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Chitra Express, Sundarban Express and Jahanabad Express
- Dhaka to Khulna train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-khulna
- Where to stay: Hotels in the city Tk 1,200-4,000 (approx.); Sundarbans launch tour packages Tk 7,000-15,000 per person (approx.)
- What to eat: Mutton cooked with chuijhal (a spicy vine), Rupsha prawns
- Tips: You need a permit to go deep into the Sundarbans; go with an approved tour operator

What to see:

1. Sundarbans (Karamjal): The world's largest mangrove forest; deer, crocodiles and a wooden walkway at Karamjal, and you can go and come back the same day
2. Hiron Point & Kotka: A 2-3 day launch tour deep into the Sundarbans; tiger pugmarks, herds of deer and Kotka beach
3. Rupsha Bridge: The Khan Jahan Ali Bridge; evening walks along the Rupsha River and boat rides
4. Khulna Divisional Museum: A small but well-organised museum in the middle of the city; archaeological finds and the history of Bagerhat
5. Dacope Eco Park: An eco park on the edge of the Sundarbans; views of the forest from the watchtower
6. Shaheed Hadis Park: An old park in the heart of the city; a lake and a place for evening hangouts

### Kushtia

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/kushtia
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Kushtia
- Best time: October to March (Lalon festivals in October and March)
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 3.5-4 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge), by train via Poradah
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Madhumati Express, Chitra Express, Sundarban Express and Benapole Express
- Dhaka to Kushtia train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-kushtia
- Where to stay: Hotels in town, Tk 1,000-3,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Kushtia's tiler khaja (sesame sweet), kulfi malai (milk ice cream)
- Tips: If you go at the time of the Lalon fair, book your hotel in advance

What to see:

1. Lalon Shah Shrine: The tomb of Lalon, emperor of the Bauls; songs in the evening, and huge fairs at Dol Purnima and in Kartik (October-November)
2. Shilaidaha Kuthibari: Rabindranath's zamindari house on the bank of the Padma; many of the songs of Gitanjali were written here
3. Hardinge Bridge: A century-old railway bridge over the Padma at Pakshi; watch it from the riverbank at sunset
4. Mir Mosharraf Hossain House: The house and memorial museum of the author of 'Bishad Sindhu', at Lahinipara
5. Mohini Mill: A huge British-era textile mill; old architecture and history
6. Gorai River: The Gorai River right beside the town; afternoon boat rides and views of the chars

### Magura

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/magura
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Magura
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 3-3.5 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Magura's kumror bori (sun-dried pumpkin dumplings), date palm juice
- Tips: You can see it in half a day on the way to Jashore or Kushtia

What to see:

1. Siddheshwari Math: An old Shiva temple and math (tower temple) beside the Atharobanki River
2. Gorai Bridge: A bridge over the Gorai River at Kamarkhali; a place for an afternoon outing
3. Raja Sitaram Ray Palace: A 17th-century capital at Mohammadpur; the Dashabhuja temple and a huge pond
4. Nomani Maidan: A field in the middle of town; Magura's famous kumror bori and sweets
5. Farrukh Ahmad's Home: The birthplace of Farrukh Ahmad, poet of 'Panjeri', in Majhail village, Sreepur upazila
6. Sreepur Zamindar Bari: An old zamindar house in Sreepur upazila; its name is linked to Rabindranath's novel 'Bou Thakuranir Haat'

### Meherpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/meherpur
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Meherpur
- Best time: November to February; May to June for mangoes
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4.5-5 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Meherpur's Himsagar mangoes, Sabitri sweets
- Tips: Mujibnagar holds a huge event on 17 April, and it is very crowded that day

What to see:

1. Mujibnagar Memorial: Where the first government took its oath on 17 April 1971; a mango grove, a memorial and Liberation War sculptures
2. Amjhupi Neelkuthi: The house of British indigo planters beside the Kajla River; an old building in shady grounds
3. Bhatpara Neelkuthi: Another indigo planters' house, on the bank of the Mathabhanga River in Gangni; now an eco park
4. Meherpur Mango Orchards: Orchards full of Himsagar mangoes in the summer mango season; Meherpur's mangoes are famous
5. Bhabarpara Catholic Church: A Catholic church about 100 years old in Bhabarpara village, Mujibnagar

### Narail

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/narail
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Narail
- Best time: November to February (Sultan Mela in January)
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 3.5-4 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Jahanabad Express and Ruposhi Bangla Express
- Dhaka to Narail train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-narail
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 800-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Narail's date palm molasses (khejur gur), pera sandesh (milk fudge)
- Tips: The Sultan museum may be closed on Fridays, so check first

What to see:

1. S M Sultan Gallery: The artist Sultan's house and gallery on the bank of the Chitra; his huge canvases and the Shishu Swarga boat
2. Chitra River: A calm river, afternoons on a boat; the backdrop of Sultan's paintings
3. Niribili Picnic Spot: A big picnic centre in Lohagara; a lake, gardens and children's rides
4. Narail Zamindar Bari: Ruins of old zamindar buildings at a ghat on the Chitra
5. Jor Bangla Temple, Lohagara: An 18th-century jor bangla temple on the bank of the Nabaganga at Raygram, Lohagara; beside it, a Shiva temple from the same period
6. Hatbaria Zamindar Bari: Traces of a zamindar house on the bank of the Chitra at Hatbaria, Sadar; a temple and a paved pond ghat survive

### Satkhira

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/satkhira
- Division: Khulna Division
- District town: Satkhira
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Where to stay: Hotels in town Tk 800-2,500 (approx.); community tourism resorts in Munshiganj
- What to eat: Satkhira's sandesh (milk sweet), prawns, honey
- Tips: For the Sundarbans you need a Forest Department permit and a guide; these can be arranged from Burigoalini

What to see:

1. Kalagachhia Sundarbans: The western part of the Sundarbans by trawler from Munshiganj; monkeys, deer and silent creeks
2. Mandarbaria Beach: A secluded beach inside the Sundarbans; the Bay of Bengal at the end of a day-long boat journey
3. Jahajghata: Villages on the edge of the Sundarbans; the lives of honey collectors (mawals) and fishers, and views of the forest
4. Probajpur Mosque: A small Mughal-era mosque in Kaliganj; fine brickwork
5. Nalta Sharif: The shrine of Khan Bahadur Ahsanullah; the country's biggest iftar in Ramadan
6. Jeshoreshwari Temple: One of the 51 Shakti Peethas, in Shyamnagar; a historic temple

### Barguna

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/barguna
- Division: Barishal Division
- District town: Barguna
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 10-12 hours overnight by launch (Sadarghat), 6-7 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town and in Patharghata, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Patharghata's sea fish, shutki (dried fish)
- Tips: Add Taltali and Shuvo Sandhya to a Kuakata tour and you can do both in one trip

What to see:

1. Haringhata Forest: A mangrove forest in Patharghata, a wooden walkway and a secluded char on the estuary
2. Shuvo Sandhya Beach: A beach ringed by casuarina woods on the Bay of Bengal at Taltali; superb sunsets
3. Tengragiri Sanctuary: A protected forest at the eastern edge of the Sundarbans; deer and birds
4. Bihongo Island: An island of birds at the mouth of the Baleshwar River; thousands of migratory birds in winter
5. Taltali Rakhine Village: A village of the Rakhine community, a Buddhist temple and handwoven cloth

### Barishal

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/barishal
- Division: Barishal Division
- District town: Barishal
- Best time: November to February; guava market July to August
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 8-9 hours overnight by launch (Sadarghat), 4 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Where to stay: Hotels in the city, Tk 1,000-3,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Barishal's hilsa, amra (hog plums) and guavas from the floating market
- Tips: If you want a cabin on the launch, book it the day before; travelling by river is a different experience

What to see:

1. Floating Guava Market: A guava market on boats in the canals of Banaripara-Bhimruli; best in July-August
2. Durga Sagar: A huge 250-year-old pond at Madhabpasha; migratory birds in winter
3. Guthia Mosque: The Baitul Aman Jame Mosque complex; a striking building of white marble
4. Kirtankhola River: The lifeblood of Barishal; huge launches at the ghat in the evening and the river breeze
5. Oxford Mission Church: A century-old red-brick church on Bogura Road; one of the most beautiful in Asia
6. Lakutia Zamindar Bari: An old zamindar house, a Shiva temple and a pond near the city

### Bhola

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/bhola
- Division: Barishal Division
- District town: Bhola
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 8-10 hours overnight by launch (from Sadarghat to Bhola/Char Fasson)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in Bhola and Char Fasson; a rest house or tent on Kukri-Mukri
- What to eat: Meghna hilsa, buffalo milk yoghurt
- Tips: Trawlers to Kukri-Mukri depend on the tides, so check the times before you go

What to see:

1. Char Kukri Mukri: Mangroves and a secluded beach in the south of the island; nights in a tent, migratory birds in winter
2. Monpura Island: A peaceful island in the middle of the Meghna; sunsets, deer and the life of fishers
3. Tarua Beach: A completely secluded sea beach further south of Kukri-Mukri
4. Dhalchar: An island of fishers at the mouth of the Bay of Bengal; dried-fish villages and the sea
5. Jacob Tower: A 225-foot watchtower in Char Fasson; chars and rivers from the top
6. Nizam Hasina Mosque: A striking modern mosque in Bhola town

### Jhalokati

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/jhalokati
- Division: Barishal Division
- District town: Jhalokati
- Best time: July to August (guavas), winter for the town
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 8-9 hours overnight by launch, 4-4.5 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge); 45 minutes from Barishal
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town; it is easy to stay in Barishal and visit for the day
- What to eat: Jhalokati's guavas, amra (hog plums), villages of shital pati (cool reed mats)
- Tips: Bhimruli is 1 hour from Barishal by auto-rickshaw; go very early in the morning

What to see:

1. Bhimruli Floating Market: The country's most famous floating market; guavas on hundreds of boats, and orchards on both banks of the canal
2. Kirtipasha Zamindar Bari: A 19th-century zamindar house and temple near Jhalokati town
3. Sujabad Fort: Ruins of a Mughal-era fort near the Sugandha River
4. Gabkhan Bridge: The Gabkhan Channel, known as the Suez of Bengal; views of the waterway from the bridge
5. Dhansiri River: The very Dhansiri of Jibanananda's poetry; quiet afternoons on a boat

### Patuakhali

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/patuakhali
- Division: Barishal Division
- District town: Patuakhali
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by direct bus to Kuakata (via the Padma Bridge); by launch to Patuakhali
- Where to stay: Hotels in Kuakata Tk 1,000-5,000 (approx.); better to stay near the beach
- What to eat: Kuakata's fried crab, shutki (dried fish), Rakhine food
- Tips: You can ride a motorbike along the beach to Gangamati and Lebur Char in a day; agree the fare before you get on

What to see:

1. Kuakata Beach: Sagar Kanya, the 'daughter of the sea'; you can watch both sunrise and sunset from the same beach
2. Gangamati: A secluded beach east of Kuakata, full of casuarina woods and red crabs
3. Fatrar Char: The eastern part of the Sundarbans by trawler from Kuakata; mangroves and silence
4. Rakhine Village: A Rakhine village at Mishripara, handlooms and a huge Buddha statue
5. Lebur Char: The best place to watch the sunset, west of Kuakata; freshly fried crab
6. Payra Bridge: A striking bridge at Lebukhali; the country's third seaport

### Pirojpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/pirojpur
- Division: Barishal Division
- District town: Pirojpur
- Best time: July to September for the floating market; otherwise winter
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 9-10 hours overnight by launch (Hularhat), 5 hours by bus (via the Padma Bridge)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Pirojpur's guavas, amra (hog plums), coconut sweets
- Tips: The floating market is busiest from 8 to 10 am; stay the night before in Banaripara or Swarupkathi

What to see:

1. Swarupkathi Floating Market: A guava and amra market on boats in the canals of Atghar-Kuriana; boat rides through the orchards
2. Rayerkathi Zamindar Bari: An old zamindar house and a row of temples near the town
3. Hularhat: The ghat where launches from Dhaka land; the wide banks of the Kocha River
4. Momin Mosque: A unique wooden mosque, with carved woodwork made without nails
5. Bhandaria Park: A park for family outings in the upazila town

### Habiganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/habiganj
- Division: Sylhet Division
- District town: Habiganj
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (from Sayedabad), 4-5 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Parabat Express, Jayentika Express, Upaban Express and Kalni Express
- Dhaka to Shaistaganj train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-shaistaganj
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Habiganj Sadar, Tk 1,000-2,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Habiganj's shatkora (a citrus fruit), tea and pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: Before entering Satchari, find out about the Forest Department's tickets and rules

What to see:

1. Satchari National Park: Dense forest in Chunarughat, where you can see monkeys and birds
2. Rema-Kalenga Wildlife Sanctuary: A vast forest area in Chunarughat, with a chance to see wildlife and birds
3. Baniachong: Asia's largest village; the Bithangal Akhra (Vaishnava monastery), Kamalarani's pond and haor views
4. Teliapara Tea Estate: A green hillside tea garden in Chunarughat, with peaceful surroundings
5. Shankarpasha Shahi Mosque: A historic Sultanate-era mosque near Habiganj Sadar

### Moulvibazar

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/moulvibazar
- Division: Sylhet Division
- District town: Moulvibazar
- Best time: October to March (June to September for Madhabkunda)
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Sayedabad/Kamalapur), 4-5 hours by train (Sreemangal)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Parabat Express, Jayentika Express, Upaban Express and Kalni Express
- Dhaka to Sreemangal train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-sreemangal
- Where to stay: Resorts and hotels in Sreemangal, Tk 1,500-6,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Seven-layer tea, pineapples and pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: Go to Lawachara early in the morning; you have a better chance of seeing wildlife

What to see:

1. Sreemangal Tea Gardens: Tea gardens spread over green hillocks, and a chance to see the lives of tea workers
2. Lawachara National Park: A national park famous for its dense forest, hoolock gibbons and birds
3. Madhabkunda Waterfall: The country's highest waterfall, in Barlekha; at its most beautiful in the monsoon
4. Madhabpur Lake: A beautiful lake ringed by Sreemangal's tea gardens, with birds all around
5. Nilkantha Tea Cabin: Sreemangal's famous seven-layer tea cabin
6. Hakaluki Haor: One of the country's largest haors (wetlands); a gathering of migratory birds in winter

### Sunamganj

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/sunamganj
- Division: Sylhet Division
- District town: Sunamganj
- Best time: July to October (monsoon), November to February
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 7-8 hours by bus (from Sayedabad/Gabtoli), 7 hours by train (via Sylhet)
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in Sunamganj Tk 800-2,000 (approx.), houseboats on the haor Tk 1,000-3,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Fish from the haor and Sunamganj's yoghurt
- Tips: For a haor trip, book your boat in advance; storms make it risky in the monsoon

What to see:

1. Tanguar Haor: A unique haor (wetland): vast waters in the monsoon, thousands of birds and the life of fishers
2. Niladri Lake: A man-made lake of blue water ringed by hills, at Tekerghat
3. Barek Tila: A high hillock beside Tanguar Haor, with views of the haor and the hills
4. Jadukata River: A clear hill river in Tahirpur; stones and sandbanks in winter
5. Shimul Bagan: A garden of red flowers in Tahirpur when the shimul (silk cotton) trees bloom
6. Shanir Haor: A wide haor in the Dharmapasha-Tahirpur area, calm and less crowded

### Sylhet

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/sylhet
- Division: Sylhet Division
- District town: Sylhet
- Best time: October to March (June to September for Ratargul)
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Sayedabad/Kamalapur), 6-7 hours by train, 50 minutes by air
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Parabat Express, Jayentika Express, Upaban Express and Kalni Express
- Dhaka to Sylhet train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-sylhet
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Sylhet city, Tk 1,500-4,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Sylheti seven-layer tea, shatkora (a citrus fruit) and akhni (spiced meat rice)
- Tips: Allow 2 days to see Jaflong, Sada Pathor and Bichanakandi together

What to see:

1. Jaflong: A border tourist spot surrounded by hills, waterfalls and the clear water of the Piyain River
2. Ratargul Swamp Forest: The country's only freshwater swamp forest; explore it by boat in the monsoon
3. Bichanakandi: Stones and streams of clear water in Companiganj, with the Meghalaya hills in front
4. Hazrat Shah Jalal Dargah: The main historic shrine and religious centre of Sylhet city
5. Lalakhal: A river of clear green water; boat trips, and views beside the tea gardens in the monsoon
6. Sada Pathor: A wide stretch of water over white stones in the Dhopagaon area, a popular place for photos

### Dinajpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/dinajpur
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Dinajpur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 7-8 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), 9-10 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express, Panchagarh Express, Nilsagar Express, Chilahati Express and Kurigram Express
- Dhaka to Dinajpur train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-dinajpur
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in town, Tk 1,000-3,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Dinajpur's Katarivog rice (fragrant rice), lychees and bhuna khichuri (spiced rice and lentils)
- Tips: See Kantajew and Nayabad together; the light is better in the morning

What to see:

1. Kantajew Temple: An 18th-century navaratna (nine-spired) temple decorated with terracotta, one of the finest temples in the country
2. Ramsagar: The country's largest man-made pond, with a national park and a picnic spot beside it
3. Nayabad Mosque: An ornate historic mosque close to the Kantajew Temple
4. Sitakot Vihara: Ruins of an ancient Buddhist monastery (vihara) in Nawabganj
5. Dinajpur Rajbari: The buildings of Maharaja Pran Nath Roy's historic palace
6. Shopnopuri: A popular amusement park near Dinajpur town for a family outing

### Gaibandha

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/gaibandha
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Gaibandha
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 6-7 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 7-8 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Lalmoni Express, Rangpur Express and Burimari Express
- Dhaka to Gaibandha train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-gaibandha
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Gaibandha's pitha (rice cakes) and river fish
- Tips: Hire a local boat to go to the chars; getting around can be hard in the monsoon

What to see:

1. Balashi Ghat: An old ferry ghat on the Jamuna; the vast river and its chars
2. Friendship Centre: World-famous, Aga Khan Award-winning architecture by architect Kashef Chowdhury, at Kashim Bazar
3. Bardhan Kuthi: Ruins of an old palace in Gobindaganj
4. Jamuna Chars: Char villages by boat from Fulchhari; a look at life on the chars
5. Birat Raja's Mound: The mound of an ancient fort city at Rajahar, Gobindaganj; a month-long pilgrimage fair is held in Boishakh (April-May)
6. Naldanga Zamindar Bari: Ruins of the Lahiri zamindars' house at Naldanga, Sadullapur; two temples, a well and a huge pond survive

### Kurigram

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/kurigram
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Kurigram
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 8-9 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 10 hours by train (via Rangpur)
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Kurigram Express
- Dhaka to Kurigram train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-kurigram
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in Kurigram Sadar, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Kurigram's river fish and pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: There is little local transport to Chilmari, so set off in the morning

What to see:

1. Chilmari River Port: The vast banks of the Brahmaputra; the very ghat from Abbasuddin's song
2. Brahmaputra Chars: Char villages by boat; life on the chars and the vastness of the river
3. Chandamari Mosque: A three-domed Mughal-era mosque in Rajarhat
4. Dharla Bridge: The Dharla River beside the town; the sunset from the bridge in the evening
5. Sonahat Land Port: A land port on the Indian border in Bhurungamari, and the British-era Sonahat Bridge

### Lalmonirhat

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/lalmonirhat
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Lalmonirhat
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 9-10 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 8-9 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Lalmoni Express and Burimari Express
- Dhaka to Lalmonirhat train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-lalmonirhat
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Lalmonirhat's fish from the Teesta and boiled-egg khichuri (rice and lentils)
- Tips: To enter Dahagram, follow the BGB (border guard) rules and carry your national ID card

What to see:

1. Tin Bigha Corridor: The historic corridor in Patgram that leads to Dahagram-Angarpota
2. Burimari Land Port: An important land port on the Patgram border
3. Tista Railway Bridge: A historic railway bridge over the Teesta River, where the river spreads out like a huge canvas
4. Lalmonirhat Railway Junction: A century-old railway junction and an old locomotive workshop
5. Lalmonirhat Airport: An old airbase from the Second World War

### Nilphamari

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/nilphamari
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Nilphamari
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 7-8 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), by train or air via Saidpur
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Nilsagar Express and Chilahati Express
- Dhaka to Nilphamari train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-nilphamari
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in Saidpur and Nilphamari, Tk 1,000-2,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Saidpur's sandesh (milk sweet) and kebabs
- Tips: To get there fast, fly from Dhaka to Saidpur; the rest of the way is short

What to see:

1. Teesta Barrage: The country's largest irrigation project; the vast waters of the Teesta and afternoon crowds
2. Neelsagar: A huge ancient pond in Sadar; migratory birds in winter, and a picnic spot
3. Chini Mosque: A mosque with unique decoration, covered in pieces of china
4. Saidpur Railway Workshop: A British railway workshop from 1870, the largest in the country
5. Dharmapal's Fort: Remains of an ancient fort with earthen walls on the east bank of the Deonai River in Jaldhaka, known by the name of the Pala king Dharmapala

### Panchagarh

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/panchagarh
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Panchagarh
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 3 days
- From Dhaka: 9-10 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), 10-11 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express and Panchagarh Express
- Dhaka to Panchagarh train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-panchagarh
- Where to stay: Resorts and hotels in Panchagarh and Tetulia, Tk 1,500-5,000 (approx.)
- What to eat: Panchagarh's tea, Rangpur-style food and duck
- Tips: Go at dawn in winter to see Kanchenjunga; you get a good view when it is not hidden by fog

What to see:

1. Tetulia Dak Bungalow: A historic dak bungalow (rest house) at the far northern tip of Bangladesh
2. Kanchenjunga View Point: On clear winter mornings, Mount Kanchenjunga can be seen from Tetulia
3. Banglabandha Land Port: The country's northernmost land port; the special feeling of standing at the zero line
4. Bhitargarh Fort: The huge earthen walls and ruins of an ancient fort city
5. Tetulia Tea Gardens: Flatland tea gardens; green views with the mountains in the background
6. Mahananda River: A calm river in winter near Tetulia, with views of its sandbanks

### Rangpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/rangpur
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Rangpur
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 7-8 hours by bus (from Gabtoli/Kalyanpur), 9-10 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Rangpur Express, Kurigram Express, Lalmoni Express and Burimari Express
- Dhaka to Rangpur train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-rangpur
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in the city, Tk 1,200-3,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Rangpur's Haribhanga mangoes, bhorta (mashed relishes) and bhuna khichuri (spiced rice and lentils)
- Tips: You can see Tajhat and Carmichael College in one day

What to see:

1. Tajhat Palace: Rangpur's historic royal palace, now a museum
2. Carmichael College: An old college of North Bengal; its historic buildings are worth seeing
3. Pairaband, Begum Rokeya's Home: The birthplace of Begum Rokeya, pioneer of women's education, in Mithapukur
4. Rangpur Zoo: A popular place near the city for a family outing
5. Vinnya Jagat Park: A big amusement park at Ganjipur in Khaleya union, Sadar upazila; a popular place for a family outing
6. Chikli Beel & Park: A park around the century-old Chikli Beel, north of the city; migratory birds in winter and a fountain of coloured lights at night

### Thakurgaon

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/thakurgaon
- Division: Rangpur Division
- District town: Thakurgaon
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 9-10 hours by bus (from Gabtoli), 11 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Ekota Express, Drutojan Express and Panchagarh Express
- Dhaka to Thakurgaon train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-thakurgaon
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Thakurgaon's tea and biscuits, and pitha (rice cakes)
- Tips: Plan it together with a trip to Panchagarh and Dinajpur

What to see:

1. Surjapuri Mango Tree: Asia's largest mango tree, its branches spreading over two bighas (a local land unit); 200 years old
2. Ramrai Dighi: A huge ancient pond in Ranisankail; thousands of migratory birds in winter
3. Haripur Rajbari: A 19th-century zamindar palace in Haripur
4. Jamalpur Zamindar Mosque: An ornate old mosque and zamindar house in Sadar
5. Nekmarad Mazar: A traditional shrine in Ranisankail; a month-long fair in Chaitra (March-April)

### Jamalpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/jamalpur
- Division: Mymensingh Division
- District town: Jamalpur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 4-5 hours by bus (from Mohakhali/Gabtoli), 5-6 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Tista Express, Bhrammaputra Express, Aghnibina Express, Jamuna Express and Jamalpur Express
- Dhaka to Jamalpur train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-jamalpur
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 700-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Jamalpur's pitha (rice cakes) and fish from the Jamuna
- Tips: It is a small town, so ask local people for advice before you head out

What to see:

1. Shah Jamal Mazar: The saint Jamalpur is named after; his shrine and a mosque in the town centre
2. Lauchapra Hills: A recreation centre at the foot of the Garo Hills in Bakshiganj; rows of hills from the watchtower
3. Gandhi Ashram: Memories of Gandhi and a museum at the ashram in Kajla
4. Dayamoyee Temple: A 300-year-old temple in Jamalpur town
5. Jamuna Char: Jamuna chars in Dewanganj; watch Jamalpur's famous nakshi kantha (embroidered quilts) being made by hand

### Mymensingh

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/mymensingh
- Division: Mymensingh Division
- District town: Mymensingh
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 3-4 hours by bus (from Mohakhali), 3-4 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Tista Express, Bhrammaputra Express, Aghnibina Express, Jamuna Express, Jamalpur Express, Hawr Express and Mohonganj Express
- Dhaka to Mymensingh train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-mymensingh
- Where to stay: Mid-range hotels in the city, Tk 1,200-3,500 (approx.)
- What to eat: Muktagacha's monda (milk sweet), Mymensingh's puli pitha (stuffed rice dumplings)
- Tips: Go early in the morning to buy Muktagacha's monda; the good ones sell out fast

What to see:

1. Shashi Lodge: The historic palace of Maharaja Shashikanta in the centre of Mymensingh city
2. Alexander Castle: A beautiful historic building in the English style on the bank of the Brahmaputra
3. Muktagacha Zamindar Bari: The huge historic zamindar palace of Raja Jagat Kishore
4. Zainul Abedin Museum: A collection of paintings and mementoes of Shilpacharya (great master) Zainul Abedin
5. Brahmaputra River: The famous river flowing past the city; a place to sit by the ghat in the afternoon
6. Bangladesh Agricultural University: A huge green campus, lovely for an afternoon walk

### Netrokona

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/netrokona
- Division: Mymensingh Division
- District town: Netrokona
- Best time: November to February
- Days needed: 2 days
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Mohakhali), about 4.5 hours by train
- Trains from Dhaka that stop in this district: Hawr Express and Mohonganj Express
- Dhaka to Netrokona train timetable: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/train/dhaka-netrokona
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in Netrokona and Durgapur, Tk 600-1,800 (approx.)
- What to eat: Netrokona's balish mishti ('pillow' sweet) and food of the hill areas
- Tips: You can see the Durgapur area in one day; hire a local vehicle

What to see:

1. Birishiri Cultural Academy: A centre in Durgapur showing the culture and way of life of the Garo and Hajong peoples
2. Bijoypur China Clay Hills: Hills of white clay and lakes of blue water in Durgapur, popular for photos
3. Someshwari River: A clear hill river near Birishiri; sandbanks and stones show in winter
4. Kamalarani Sagar Dighi: A huge ancient pond in Durgapur, tied to the memory of Queen Kamala
5. Ranikhong Mission: A Catholic mission in Durgapur and the calm of a Garo village

### Sherpur

- Guide: https://ghuredekhabangladesh.com/en/jela/sherpur
- Division: Mymensingh Division
- District town: Sherpur
- Best time: October to March
- Days needed: 1 day
- From Dhaka: 5-6 hours by bus (from Mohakhali/Gabtoli), 6 hours by train
- Where to stay: Basic hotels in town, Tk 600-1,600 (approx.)
- What to eat: Sherpur's pitha (rice cakes) and Garo food
- Tips: You can see Gajni and Madhutila in one day; set off in the morning

What to see:

1. Gajni Resort: A lake, a hanging bridge and a watchtower in the lap of the Garo Hills, in Jhenaigati
2. Madhutila Eco Park: An eco park in the hill forest of Nalitabari; the hills of Meghalaya across the border
3. Rajar Pahar: A hill rising from the plains in Sreebardi; Garo villages and views
4. Maisaheba Mosque: A 200-year-old mosque in Sherpur town
5. Panihata-Tarani Hills: A hilly area along the border in Nalitabari upazila; the Panihata Christian mission is nearby
